title: Build Log: A focus timer web app, Step by Step

segments.narration: This is a focus timer web app, built from an empty folder by a build agent, while I recorded the screen. The finished app is 153 lines in 3 files across 3 commits. Here's how it came together, step by step.

claims.text: The finished app is 153 lines in 3 files across 3 commits.

segments.narration: First: layout and styling. The goal: show a 25:00 timer, a label and Start / Reset buttons, centred, dark theme. Get the layout right first, so the logic later has stable element ids to hook into. This commit changed 2 files, adding 57 lines and removing 0.

claims.text: The goal: show a 25:00 timer, a label and Start / Reset buttons, centred, dark theme.
Get the layout right first, so the logic later has stable element ids to hook into.
This commit changed 2 files, adding 57 lines and removing 0.

segments.narration: Next: countdown logic. The goal: start/pause toggles a countdown that updates once per second; Reset returns to 25:00. The timer measures elapsed time against a start timestamp instead of counting ticks, so it stays accurate when the browser throttles background tabs. This commit changed 2 files, adding 57 lines and removing 0.

segments.narration: Finally: progress ring, sessions and shortcuts. The goal: add an SVG progress ring, a completed-session counter saved in localStorage and a Space-bar shortcut. A ring shows progress at a glance, and the keyboard shortcut means you never need the mouse while focusing. This commit changed 3 files, adding 40 lines and removing 1.
